chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Hasan from Zur'ah said:

I asked him about a man who was prevented (from completing Hajj), and he said: 'Let him send his offering (hady) if he is with his companions, and its place is that the offering reaches its place, and its place is Mina on the Day of Sacrifice if it is in Hajj. And if it is in Umrah, he sacrifices in Mecca, and he is only required to appoint a day for them. When that day comes, he has fulfilled it. And if they differ regarding the appointed time, it does not harm him, if God wills.'

And whoever sends his offering as a voluntary offering, let him appoint a day for his companions in which he ties the necks of the animals, then let him avoid all that the person in Ihram avoids from clothing, women, perfume, and other things, except that he does not recite the Talbiyah. If he does any of that, the expiation is upon him like the expiation of the person in Ihram.

key_terms.يَوْمَ النَّحْرِ: The Day of Sacrifice (10th of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.يُقَلِّدُهُ: He ties the necks (of the sacrificial animals)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for sending the Hajj offering if a pilgrim is prevented from completing the ritual?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of the *muhsar* (one prevented from completing Hajj), distinguishing between the mandatory sacrifice location for Hajj (Mina) versus Umrah (Mecca). It further elaborates on the status of voluntary offerings (*hady* al-tatawwu'), noting that while they are exempt from the specific *talbiyah*, they must observe Ihram prohibitions and incur expiation for violations, reflecting the juristic nuance between obligatory and voluntary ritual states.
